params.description: Return only historic process instances that were finished after this date.

params.name: finishedBefore

params.name: startedAfter
params.description: Return only historic process instances that were started after this date.

params.name: startedBefore
params.description: Return only historic process instances that were started before this date.

params.name: startedBy
params.description: Return only historic process instances that were started by this user.

params.name: includeProcessVariables
params.description: An indication if the historic process instance variables should be returned as well.

params.name: includeProcessVariablesName
params.description: Indication to include process variables with the given names in the result.

params.name: callbackId
params.description: Only return instances with the given callbackId.

params.name: callbackIds

params.name: callbackType
params.description: Only return instances with the given callbackType.

params.name: parentCaseInstanceId
params.description: Only return instances with the given parent case instance id.

params.name: withoutCallbackId
params.description: Only return instances that do not have a callbackId.

params.name: tenantId
params.description: Only return instances with the given tenantId.

params.name: tenantIdLike
params.description: Only return instances with a tenant id like the given value.

params.name: tenantIdLikeIgnoreCase
params.description: Only return instances with a tenant id like the given value ignoring case.

params.name: withoutTenantId
params.description: If true, only returns instances without a tenantId set. If false, the withoutTenantId parameter is ignored.

info.name: Get the binary data for a historic process instance variable

items.docs: The response body contains the binary value of the variable. When the variable is of type binary, the content-type of the response is set to application/octet-stream, regardless of the content of the variable or the request accept-type header. In case of serializable, application/x-java-serialized-object is used as content-type.

All supported JSON parameter fields allowed are exactly the same as the parameters found for getting a collection of historic process instances, but passed in as JSON-body arguments rather than URL-parameters to allow for more advanced querying and preventing errors with request-uri’s that are too long. On top of that, the query allows for filtering based on process variables. The variables property is a JSON-array containing objects with the format as described here.
